correctness.rationale: An intra-part jump on K_(a,b) leaves opposite-neighbor proportions and type occupancy counts unchanged. For a move of type t from B into vacant A, with A_t=x and B_t=y beforehand, the utility gain is x/(a-1)-(y-1)/(b-1), which exactly matches the two changes in normalized binomial within-type counts. The mirror orientation is symmetric; any fixed agents just remove permissible transitions. Phi lies in [0,(a+b-2)/2] on a grid of spacing 1/lcm(a-1,b-1), so every strict increase moves at least one grid unit and terminates within claimed steps. Independently checked 10394 legal moves across four small parameter triples including nonregular graphs.

originality.rationale: Narayanan–Sabbagh–Voudouris 2025 full accessible article gives potentiality on regular graphs with one vacancy (Theorem 5.1) and spider graphs (Theorem 4.8), expressly proposing bipartite topologies in Section 7. The nonregular K_(a,b) with a != b and both sides >=2 is neither a regular graph nor a spider, so the paper does not imply this new exact pair-count potential and cubic bound; balanced complete bipartite and star boundary are correctly excluded as prior-covered special cases. Distinct variety-seeking and swap games use different utilities/moves.

value.rationale: Exact potential for a natural nonregular cyclic bipartite network extends known potentiality classes and gives a uniform polynomial bound independent of types and immobile agents, resolving a motivated game-dynamics gap in a setting explicitly proposed by the prior article.

final_claim: For diversity-seeking jumps on K_(a,b) with a,b>=2 and exactly one vacancy, the within-type pair-count potential Phi=sum_t binom(A_t,2)/(a-1)+binom(B_t,2)/(b-1) changes by exactly the moving agent utility gain for every feasible jump; every strict improvement sequence has length at most floor((a+b-2)*lcm(a-1,b-1)/2), thus at most (a+b-2)^3/8.
limitations: Finite bounded computational checks do not establish a universal theorem; correctness is based on the reconstructed analytical proof.
